quotes.text: I think in the era of AI, the responsible use of technology is going to become the most important thing, apart from all the skills that we should focus on.
quotes.speaker: Tracy van der Schyff
quotes.why: Frames responsible use as the core skill of the AI era.

quotes.text: And whether it's co-pilot or whatever it might be, as I mentioned, it doesn't fix things, it amplifies. So, if you had a healthy environment, it's going to amplify that healthy environment.
quotes.speaker: Tracy van der Schyff
quotes.why: Captures the guest's central thesis that Copilot amplifies existing conditions.

quotes.text: I think the first thing we need to realize is that change management is a lifelong commitment. And a lot of companies get that wrong. We need people and companies that focus on it permanently.
quotes.speaker: Tracy van der Schyff
quotes.why: Clear recommendation to treat change management as permanent, not a project.

quotes.text: We need to stop telling people what to do. We need to explain to them why it's good for them. Because if you explain to someone why it's good for them, they'll start following on their own as well.
quotes.speaker: Tracy van der Schyff
quotes.why: Practical adoption advice: explain intent instead of issuing rules.

takeaways: Digital fluency goes beyond knowing which buttons to click: people need to use tools with purpose, efficiently and responsibly, and that now includes AI.
Copilot does not fix a messy Microsoft 365 environment; it amplifies what is already there, so storage habits, sharing and permissions have to be addressed first.
Change management works only as a permanent part of the company's strategy, explaining to people why practices matter rather than just telling them what to do.
hook: Many organizations switch on Copilot and expect it to fix a chaotic Microsoft 365 environment. In this conversation, Mirko Peters and Tracy van der Schyff discuss digital fluency, the Me, We, Us model, ontological design and permanent change management for adoption leads, IT managers and business leaders. You will learn why investing in people matters more than adding another tool.
